title: Harmonic removal can mimic shared dip changes in released TESS CPV measurements
abstract: We test whether changes in different dips of the same complex periodic variable show a shared process. Released TESS per-cycle depths give mean change correlation 0.179 (95% star-bootstrap interval 0.126 to 0.233), from 468 pairs in 149 sectors of 58 stars. Independent dips injected in real control flux give similar positive correlations. We derive the phase transfer matrix caused by subtraction of harmonics 0 to 2. A conditional box inverse changes the real mean to -0.070 (-0.117 to -0.024). This is not evidence for material exchange: the inverse also gives negative noise correlations. On the selected real geometries, independent equal-variance boxes have expected direct correlation +0.253, while independent white noise has expected inverse correlation -0.122. Known Gaussian injection shapes and exact covariance checks test the method. These are processing examples, not fitted physical nulls. The released summaries do not identify shared supply or redistribution. Uniform weights, fixed box support, selected stars and unavailable full phase-bin covariance limit inference. We include code, aggregate results, source hashes and a separate-scratch reproduction script.

display.caption: Dip change correlations in real stars and independent injected dips. The conditional box inverse is a processing sensitivity, not a physical clump estimate. Bars show 95% star-bootstrap intervals.

citations.reason: Released dip-depth series and independent-dip injections. We test cross-dip relations, not its time-asymmetry result.
